findings.F1: The coin's 20-day volatility sets the size of the next-day reversal. In the coins' own top third of 20-day volatility, a down day is followed by a next-day excess return of +0.71 % (t 5.59, 2357 days) and an up day by -0.36 % (t -3.20, 2491 days). In the bottom third, down days are followed by -0.16 % (t -2.03) and up days by -0.00 % (t -0.03).
findings.F2: The reversal is graded by the size of the move times the volatility level. On down days, regressing the next-day excess return on the day's return gives t 2.63 for the return alone and t -6.64 for the return × relative volatility term (7151 days). On all days the return × relative volatility term has t -4.34 (14500 days).
findings.F3: Inside the high-volatility third, the next day follows the day's return quintile in a steady line: +1.13 % (t 5.18) after the largest falls, +0.45 % (t 2.31), -0.00 %, -0.46 % (t -2.64), and -0.32 % (t -1.59) after the largest rises, about 970 days each. In the low-volatility third, no quintile goes past +0.10 % or below -0.26 %.
findings.F4: The high-volatility reversal (next-day return signed against the day's move) is broad.
findings.F5: The tested idea's top fifth of down-day forecasts earns only when volatility is high. Next-day excess return is +1.50 % (t 6.01, 754 days) in the high-volatility third, +0.21 % (t 1.40) in the middle third and -0.13 % (t -1.04) in the low third.
findings.F6: Close location and volume still carry their own information on down days. With the volatility-scaled return in the regression, the closeness to the low × log volume ratio has t 4.38 and the volatility-scaled return itself has t 0.03 (7151 days).
findings.F7: The book earns on short holds and loses on longer ones.
findings.F8: Weekday patterns do not hold up. The pooled weekday t-values range from -2.70 to +3.76, but the same weekday's sign changes from year to year: Wednesday has t -6.99 in 2019 and +0.70 in 2021. I count this as chance, not a finding to build on.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall, and the higher its 20-day volatility against its own past level, the more it rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin for a day after a sharp fall in a turbulent market, and refuses to buy after the same fall in a calm market.
ideas.name: volatile-regime fall rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day rise, and the higher its 20-day volatility against its own past level, the more it falls over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader refuses to chase a sharp one-day rise in a turbulent market, and may sell it for a day.
ideas.name: volatile-regime rise fades

ideas.idea: The nearer a coin closes to its day's low on a down day whose volume is heavy against its prior 20-day average, the more it rises over the next day. The higher its 20-day volatility against its own past level, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys after heavy-volume falls that close at the low mainly when the coin is turbulent, and refuses them when it is calm.
ideas.name: absorption rebound in turbulence
